title: Medical Conditions Guide
description: How the UK market usually treats common medical conditions for life cover, critical illness and income protection, and what to ask the client.
status: For internal use only, not for clients. This is a general guide to how the UK market usually treats each condition, not any one insurer's underwriting. Every insurer is different and their approach changes, so always confirm with the insurer's underwriting team before you quote a client terms.
askEveryone: What was the exact diagnosis, and when?
What treatment or medication now, and any changes in the last year?
When did they last have symptoms or a flare-up?
Any time off work for it? How long, and when?
Any hospital stays, surgery or specialist referrals?
Any tests, scans or referrals still waiting? Pending investigations usually mean the insurer postpones until results are back.
Height, weight, smoking or vaping, and alcohol units per week.
Family history: parents or siblings with heart disease, stroke, cancer or diabetes before age 60.
bestTerms: Collect the details above before you quote. Vague answers lead to cautious decisions.
Run a pre-application enquiry with the underwriting helpline at 2 or 3 insurers.
Compare each product separately. The best insurer for life may not be the best for IP.
Splitting cover between insurers is fine if it gets the client better terms.
If you get a loading or exclusion, ask whether it can be reviewed after a period without symptoms.
Remind the client to answer every question fully and honestly. A wrong answer can mean a claim is reduced or not paid.
Record why you chose the insurer on the case notes.

conditions.name: Anxiety & depression
conditions.keywords: mental health anxiety depression stress ptsd sertraline citalopram fluoxetine counselling

life.note: Mild, treated, no hospital stays: usually standard. Self-harm, suicide attempt or admission: loading, postponement or decline.

ci.note: Not a core CI condition. Severe history can still affect terms.

ip.note: Mental health exclusion is common, especially with recent time off work. Mild, one-off episodes may be standard.

ask: Time off work in the last 5 years
Any self-harm, suicidal thoughts or hospital admission
conditions.tip: This is the condition where insurers differ most on IP. Shop around, and ask whether the exclusion can be reviewed after a set time without symptoms.

conditions.name: Raised blood pressure
conditions.keywords: hypertension bp blood pressure amlodipine ramipril

life.note: Treated and controlled: usually standard. High recent readings: loading.

ci.note: More sensitive than life because heart attack and stroke are core claims.

ip.note: Usually standard if controlled.

ask: Last 2 or 3 readings and their dates
Other risk factors: BMI, cholesterol, diabetes, smoking
conditions.tip: Insurers look at combined heart risk. High blood pressure with a high BMI or cholesterol can be loaded more than each alone.

conditions.name: Raised cholesterol
conditions.keywords: cholesterol statin lipids

life.note: Usually standard if treated or only mildly raised.

ci.note: Very high readings, or combined with other heart risks, can lead to a loading.

ip.note: Usually standard.

ask: Latest total cholesterol and HDL ratio
Any family history of early heart disease
conditions.tip: A reading on its own is rarely a problem. The other cardiac risk factors decide the outcome.

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes
conditions.keywords: diabetes type 2 metformin hba1c sugar insulin

life.note: Many insurers offer cover, often with a loading. Depends on control (HbA1c), age at diagnosis and complications.

ci.note: Harder to place. Loadings or decline are common, especially with complications.

ip.note: Loading or decline possible, often with exclusions.

conditions.tip: Older age at diagnosis and good HbA1c readings help a lot. Get the actual numbers before you approach insurers.

conditions.name: Type 1 diabetes
conditions.keywords: diabetes type 1 insulin hba1c hypo pump

life.note: Often available with a loading if well controlled with no complications.

ip.note: Often difficult. Decline or heavy terms are common.

conditions.tip: Life cover is usually achievable. Set expectations early on CI and IP, and consider specialist insurers if mainstream ones decline.

conditions.name: High BMI
conditions.keywords: bmi weight overweight obese obesity build

life.note: Standard up to a certain BMI at each insurer, then loadings.

ip.note: Similar, and can combine with joint or back exclusions.

ask: Linked conditions: blood pressure, diabetes, sleep apnoea, joints
conditions.tip: Use the real height and weight, not an estimate. Insurers' build limits differ, so a client loaded at one may be standard at another.

conditions.name: Asthma
conditions.keywords: asthma inhaler steroids prednisolone breathing

life.note: Mild, inhaler controlled: standard. Hospital admissions or regular oral steroids: loading.

ip.note: Severe asthma or time off work can lead to a loading or exclusion.

ask: Steroid tablet courses in the last 2 years
conditions.tip: Most asthma is standard. The questions that matter are steroid tablets and hospital visits.

conditions.name: Sleep apnoea
conditions.keywords: sleep apnoea apnea osa cpap snoring

life.note: Treated with CPAP and used regularly: often standard. Untreated: loading or postponement.

ip.note: Often standard if treated. Can be affected by occupation, e.g. drivers.

ask: Any daytime sleepiness or driving issues
conditions.tip: Proof the client uses CPAP regularly makes a big difference.

conditions.name: Back & neck pain
conditions.keywords: back neck pain sciatica disc spine whiplash physio musculoskeletal

life.note: Usually standard.

ip.note: A back or spine exclusion is common, especially with recent time off, physio or surgery.

ask: Occupation and how manual it is
conditions.tip: A single strain years ago with no time off may be standard. Ask whether the exclusion can be reviewed after a few years without symptoms.

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.keywords: arthritis osteoarthritis joint knee hip wear tear

life.note: Usually standard.

ip.note: An exclusion for the affected joint is likely, especially in manual jobs.

conditions.tip: Planned surgery usually means IP is postponed until after recovery.

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.keywords: rheumatoid arthritis ra methotrexate biologics inflammatory

life.note: Mild and stable: possibly standard. Biologic drugs or organ involvement: loading.

ci.note: Loading possible depending on severity and medication.

ip.note: Exclusion or decline is likely.

ask: Joint damage or other organs affected
conditions.tip: Do not mix this up with osteoarthritis. Insurers treat them very differently, so confirm the exact diagnosis.

conditions.name: Gout
conditions.keywords: gout allopurinol uric acid joint

life.note: Usually standard on its own.

ci.note: Usually standard unless kidney function is affected.

ip.note: A gout or joint exclusion is common. Deferral is possible with frequent attacks.

ask: Attacks per year and date of last one
conditions.tip: Gout often comes with high BMI and blood pressure. Underwriters look at the combination.

conditions.name: Underactive thyroid
conditions.keywords: thyroid hypothyroidism levothyroxine underactive overactive graves

life.note: Treated and stable: standard.

ip.note: Standard.

conditions.tip: Overactive thyroid (Graves' disease) or thyroid cancer are different and need more detail.

conditions.name: Crohn's & ulcerative colitis
conditions.keywords: crohns crohn colitis ulcerative ibd bowel

life.note: Mild and in remission: may be standard. Frequent flares, steroids or surgery: loading.

ci.note: Loading possible, partly because of the link to bowel cancer.

ip.note: An exclusion for the bowel condition is common.

conditions.tip: Make sure it is IBD and not IBS. They are very different for underwriting.

conditions.name: IBS
conditions.keywords: ibs irritable bowel stomach

life.note: Standard.

ip.note: Usually standard. An exclusion is possible with time off work.

ask: Was it confirmed by a doctor?
conditions.tip: Bowel investigations still pending will usually mean a postponement.

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.keywords: migraine headache neurology

life.note: Standard.

ip.note: An exclusion is possible if frequent or causing time off.

conditions.tip: Pending scans or a neurology referral usually means a postponement.

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.keywords: epilepsy seizure fit neurology

life.note: Well controlled with no recent seizures: standard or a small loading.

ip.note: Loading, exclusion or decline, depending on control and occupation.

conditions.tip: Date of last seizure is the single most important answer. Get it exactly.

conditions.name: Palpitations & AF
conditions.keywords: heart af atrial fibrillation palpitations arrhythmia ecg cardiac

life.note: Palpitations with normal tests: usually standard. AF: depends on type, treatment and other heart conditions.

ci.note: AF often leads to a loading.

ip.note: Loading or exclusion possible.

conditions.tip: Get the test results. "Palpitations, all tests normal" is a very different case from diagnosed AF.

conditions.name: Previous cancer
conditions.aka: Including skin cancer and abnormal smears
conditions.keywords: cancer tumour tumor remission skin bcc melanoma cin smear oncology

life.note: Depends on type, stage and time since treatment. Postponement then reducing loadings are common. Minor skin cancers are often standard.

ci.note: A cancer exclusion or postponement is common.

ip.note: Postponement or exclusion depending on type and time since treatment.

ask: Date diagnosed and date treatment ended
Follow-up and any recurrence or spread
conditions.tip: Basal cell skin cancer and cervical cell changes (CIN) are usually treated very differently from other cancers. Get the exact name from the client.

conditions.name: Raised liver tests & alcohol
conditions.keywords: alcohol liver lft fatty drinking units

life.note: Moderate drinking with normal tests: standard. Heavy drinking or abnormal tests: loading or decline.

ip.note: Loading, or an exclusion for alcohol-related claims.

ask: Any advice from a doctor to cut down
Any treatment or support for alcohol
conditions.tip: Past alcohol dependency usually means cover is postponed until the client has been alcohol-free for a few years.
